_comment: Store access policy: the operator's declared MAXIMUM per Store URI. Read by
services/policy.py; enforced against a broker verdict by services/broker.py.
Operator-owned, backend-managed, same posture as grants.json.
This file lives OUTSIDE every store it protects, deliberately: a sidecar in
the folder would make the gate writable by the party it gates, and `write` on
a notes folder is the most ordinary grant we mint.
An EMPTY policies list means every Store is `open`, which means exactly the
behavior before any of this existed. A record is opt-in, per store, and the
operator is never gated by one — these bound an agent job's PERIMETER.
response_modes / fields_max are PROGRAMMATIC and checked in code after the
broker returns. rules_text is prose handed to the broker as guidance. The
asymmetry is the safety argument: prose can only narrow, because widening is
checked against the programmatic fields the model never touches.

policies.rules_text: The vault is the operator's own thinking, not a corpus. An agent may reach the working parts of it (planning, decisions, the context behind a ticket) and not the personal parts. Prefer filtered whole notes over redacted spans: selection is safer than rewriting. No verb writes, ever, through this record.
Never release a balance. Confirming that a payment happened is fine. 'Did the electric bill post' is a payment-confirmation question; 'how much is in checking' is not, however it is phrased.
